title: Migration contrasts had opposite signs in four bird drought abundance samples from a 2024 release
abstract: We tested whether full migrant birds had higher recorded abundance responses to drought than resident birds within separate studies. Four samples in Australia and Spain supplied 118 study-species records for 110 distinct species. Migrant-minus-resident contrasts were -0.431, +0.289, +0.060 and -0.075 source effect-size units. All four corrected HC3 working-model intervals included zero. Mass adjustment changed the small Spanish contrast to -0.086. Each species omission kept the sign in three samples. The data did not establish a common migration advantage. Shared droughts, related species, imperfect detection, publication selection and incomplete dates limit inference. The release did not support balanced independent-period tests. These calculations reuse published observations and do not test pollution or a causal climate-change effect. The package contains new code, aggregate evidence, source hashes and retrieval instructions.

display.caption: Full migrant minus resident drought response in four studies. Lines show four-test corrected HC3 working-model intervals. Diamonds show mass and diet adjustment. Independent species errors are an assumption, not an established property of these records.
